questions.question: Which of the following institutes was founded by MG Ranade and GV Joshi?
questions.solution:
• Poona Sarvajanik Sabha: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
  • Fact: Founded in 1870 to serve as a bridge between the government and the people of India.

questions.question: Which of the following movements was founded in Bengal?
questions.solution:
• Ramakrishna Mission: Ramakrishna Mission
  • Detail: Founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897 at Belur Math, Bengal, to propagate the teachings of his guru.

questions.question: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the _____________of Red Fort in Delhi.
questions.solution:
• Red Fort Flag Hoisting: Lahori Gate
  • Tradition: Every year on Independence Day, the Prime Minister unfurls the tricolour at the Lahori Gate.

questions.question: ‘Mitra Mela’ was a revolutionary organisation founded by:
questions.solution:
• Mitra Mela: Vinayak Savarkar
  • History: Founded in 1899 at Nasik, it was later renamed 'Abhinav Bharat Society' in 1904.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighter lawyers from Bengal is known as Deshbandhu?
questions.solution:
• Deshbandhu: Chittaranjan Das
  • Title: 'Deshbandhu' means 'Friend of the Nation'. He was a prominent lawyer and the founder of the Swaraj Party.

questions.question: Who was the founder of Naujawan Bharat Sabha?
questions.solution:
• Naujawan Bharat Sabha: Bhagat Singh
  • 1926: Founded in Lahore to foster a revolutionary spirit among the youth by removing communalism and provincialism.

questions.question: In which year did the All-India Muslim League move a resolution demanding ‘Independent States’ for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country?
questions.solution:
• Independent States Resolution: 1940
  • Context: Better known as the 'Lahore Resolution' or the 'Pakistan Resolution,' moved by Fazlul Huq.

questions.question: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
questions.option_4: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil
questions.solution:
• Assembly Bombing (1929): Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
  • Purpose: To protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Dispute Bill. Their slogan was 'To make the deaf hear.'

questions.question: The directive principles are largely classified into three broad categories. Which of the following is NOT the part of this classification?
questions.solution:
• DPSP Classification: Authoritative
  • Civics: Directive Principles are categorized into Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles.

questions.question: Who started the temple entry movement in 1927?
questions.solution:
• Temple Entry Movement: Bhimrao Ambedkar
  • 1927: Dr. Ambedkar started this at the Kalaram Temple to challenge untouchability and caste discrimination.

questions.question: Which is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist Period?
questions.solution:
• Oldest Stupa: Sanchi Stupa
  • Architecture: Originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

questions.question: The third battle of Panipat was fought in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
• Third Battle of Panipat: 1761
  • Combatants: Fought between the Maratha Empire and the invading Afghan army of Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar?
questions.solution:
• Revolt of 1857 (Bihar): Kunwar Singh
  • Hero: An 80-year-old Zamindar of Jagdishpur who led a heroic struggle against British forces.

questions.question:
Consider the following statement about the Government of India Act, 1935.
1. This act was enacted by the British Parliament.
2. This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma Government.
3. This act was commenced from the 1 April 1935.
Select the correct statement(s) using the code given below.
questions.solution:
• GOI Act 1935: Both 1 and 2
  • Correction: While enacted by the British Parliament and separating Burma, it was mostly implemented in 1937, not April 1935.

questions.question: In which year did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal during the British rule in India?
questions.solution:
• Partition of Bengal: 1905
  • Viceroy: Lord Curzon. This led to the massive Swadeshi Movement across India.

questions.question: Visva Bharati a famous educational institute was founded in 1921 by:
questions.solution:
• Visva Bharati: Rabindranath Tagore
  • Detail: Located in Santiniketan, it was established to merge Eastern and Western philosophies.

questions.question: Who founded Bhartiya Vidya Bhavan to promote education and culture?
questions.solution:
• Bhartiya Vidya Bhavan: Dr Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi
  • 1938: Founded to preserve and promote Indian culture and values through education.

questions.question: The Bhitargaon Brick temple is a fine example of architecture of which of the following periods?
questions.solution:
• Bhitargaon Temple: Gupta period
  • Fact: Located in Kanpur, it is one of the oldest surviving terracotta/brick temples in India.

questions.question: Born on ____________, Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi whose birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti, successfully led India’s non-violence movement against the British.
questions.solution:
• Gandhi's Birth: 2 October 1869
  • Place: Porbandar, Gujarat.

questions.question: Who was the political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose?
questions.solution:
• Political Guru of Bose: Chittaranjan Das
  • Note: Bose considered C.R. Das his mentor, though he initially worked closely with Gandhi.

questions.question: Who was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi and took away an immense amount of wealth in 1739?
questions.solution:
• Nadir Shah (1739): Nadir Shah
  • Loot: He defeated the Mughals at the Battle of Karnal and took away the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

questions.question: In which state is the Sanchi Stupa situated?
questions.solution:
• Sanchi Stupa State: Madhya Pradesh
  • Location: Raisen district.

questions.question: Who had founded the first Women’s University in India?
questions.solution:
• First Women’s University: Dhondo Keshav Karve
  • 1916: SNDT Women's University was established by Maharshi Karve in Mumbai.

questions.question: 26 January was selected as the date of the inauguration of the Constitution because on the same date in 1930, the Indian National Congress had revealed ________________________________.
questions.solution:
• 26 January Significance: Purna Swaraj Movement
  • 1930: The Congress celebrated Independence Day for the first time on this date following the Lahore session.

questions.question: For which community was a journal Rast Goftar started for the purpose of social-religious reforms?
questions.solution:
• Rast Goftar: Parsis
  • Founder: Dadabhai Naoroji (1851). The title means 'The Truth Teller'.
